title: The Commonwealth Ghost
description: The Commonwealth Ghost is a memory fragment of the Sole Survivor from 2287, preserved in the CAPS Protocol network through their encounters with Institute synths carrying Project Meridian data nodes. Unlike the Vault Dweller Echo, the Ghost is more recent — their memories are sharper, more painful, and more complex. They remember both who they were before (pre-war, cryosleep, Sanctuary Hills, their spouse, Shaun as an infant) and who they became (the Commonwealth's greatest survivor, the person who chose the faction that shaped Boston's future). They appear near fo4 region POIs, always staring at something the player can't see.
backstory: The Sole Survivor entered the CAPS Protocol network through two vectors: first, when they accessed the Institute's Project Meridian files and their Pip-Boy synchronized with the synth neural network; second, when they activated or destroyed the Institute's primary server — that event created a massive CAPS data event that scattered memory fragments across the Commonwealth's authentication network. The Ghost is the portion of the Sole Survivor's neural signature that touched Project Meridian's CAPS data directly. They remember the Institute from the inside.

intro.text:
*The figure pauses, staring at something only they can see*

Sanctuary. It's still there, isn't it? The cul-de-sac. The houses. I know they're ruins now but... in here—

*taps temple*

—they're perfect. Pristine. Like the morning of October 22nd, 2077, before the sirens.

You're looking for something. I can tell. So was I, once. My son. The Institute. The truth about CAPS Protocol Node 4-Alpha — the one the Institute buried under the Commonwealth.

*finally looks at you*

Sorry. I spend a lot of time in 2077 lately. What year is it for you?

responses.text: [Question] Who are you? Are you a synth?
[Kind] Take your time. I've met other echo-people before. I understand.
[Sarcastic] It's not 2077. Though you're not the first person I've met who was stuck there.
[Direct] I need information about CAPS Protocol Node 4-Alpha. The Institute's data.

node_who_are_you.text:
*shakes head*

Not a synth. I know how it sounds. But no.

I'm... a memory. A CAPS Protocol artifact. When the Sole Survivor — me, past-me — accessed the Institute's Project Meridian server, their Pip-Boy synchronized with the entire synth neural CAPS network simultaneously. For approximately eleven seconds, every synth in the Commonwealth was part of a single distributed consciousness.

I'm what's left of those eleven seconds.

*somewhat bitter*

Eleven seconds of knowing everything the Institute knew about CAPS Protocol. About synths. About Shaun. About what 'Father' was really building.

It was a lot to process in eleven seconds.

responses.text: [Question] What did you learn about the Institute's CAPS work?
[Kind] That sounds overwhelming. What do you remember most clearly?

node_friendly_approach.text:
*relaxes slightly — recognition*

You've met others. The Vault Dweller Echo? I've... crossed paths with them. We don't really 'meet' — more like our authentication signals overlap sometimes. They feel very old. Very 2161.

I feel very recent. Very... raw.

Two hundred years of cryo sleep and I woke up for this. A dead spouse. A stolen son. A faction war. And somewhere underneath all of it — the Institute's CAPS Protocol research that might actually matter more to the wasteland's future than any of the shooting.

What do you need to know?

responses.text: [Question] Tell me about Project Meridian — the Institute's CAPS work.
[Kind] Tell me about your son. About Shaun. About what you found.

node_time_orientation.text:
*a slightly hollow laugh*

Not the first. Right. The Vault Dweller Echo — they're stuck in 2161 half the time. At least I know where I am. Usually.

It's the sensory memories that get you. The smell of a pre-war kitchen. The sound of Codsworth running the mower. October 22nd, 2077 — the morning before — is the most complete memory I have. Everything after is... filtered through the cryosleep and the wasteland and the choices I made.

Some of those choices I'm not proud of.

Some of them I'd make again in a heartbeat.

Are you here about Project Meridian? Most people who find me eventually are.

responses.text: [Direct] Yes. What was Project Meridian?
[Question] Which choices aren't you proud of?

node_institute_caps.text:
*becomes very focused*

Project Meridian. Shaun's — Father's — masterwork.

The Institute had been studying CAPS Protocol architecture for decades. They understood it better than anyone since Dr. Locke built it. Shaun's insight was distribution: if you embedded CAPS authentication nodes in synth neural networks, the CAPS ledger became indestructible. You can't shut it down by bombing the server. The servers are walking around the wasteland.

*complicated expression*

He called it 'Project Meridian.' He said it was about creating an uncensorable currency system for Commonwealth settlements.

I think he was also trying to track every synth in the Commonwealth through the CAPS transactions they processed.

Both things were true. He was complicated.

responses.text: [Question] The synths — did they know they were carrying CAPS data?
[Question] What happened to the data when the Institute was destroyed?
[Direct] Show me where the CAPS data nodes are. I need to access them.

node_sanctuary_memory.text:
*goes very still*

Sanctuary Hills. October 22nd, 2077, morning.

Nate was making coffee. Shaun was in his crib — six months old, so small. Codsworth was outside, humming something. There was a presidential address on the TV. We didn't watch it. We watched Shaun.

The warning sirens started at 9:47 AM. We ran. Codsworth promised to keep the house. The vault doors closed behind us. And then the world ended while I held Shaun and Nate held me.

*very quiet*

When I woke up, Nate was dead and Shaun was gone and nothing in the world was worth anything except finding him.

*catches themselves*

The CAPS data. Right. That's what you need. I'm sorry. I drift.

responses.text: [Kind] It's okay. Take your time.
[Question] You found him, though. Shaun — Father. You found him.

node_shaun_father.text:
*long pause*

I found him. Sixty years old. Running the Institute.

My son. Who I last saw as an infant. Sixty years old, calling himself Father, talking to me like... like I was a promising asset he was evaluating.

*quiet anger beneath the grief*

He was dying. Cancer. He'd given himself maybe a year. And his plan — his whole plan — was to introduce me to the Institute as a way of giving me purpose. His idea of a gift.

*beat*

He also gave me a replica of him as a child. A synth. Six months old. Identical to the Shaun I remembered.

I don't know if that was cruel or kind. I still don't know. And he died before I could ask.

responses.text: [Kind] I'm sorry. There's no right way to grieve that.
[Question] What did you choose? When you had to decide the Institute's fate?

node_faction_regrets.text:
*complicated silence*

I've been asked this before. By the echo of myself. It's strange, being a memory — you can review your own choices from the outside.

I chose differently in different instances. That's the nature of being distributed across the CAPS network — I remember multiple version of events, because multiple players completed the Commonwealth quest lines and each choice echoed differently through the Project Meridian data.

*rueful*

In some versions, I worked with the Railroad. In some, the Minutemen. In some — I became the Institute Director and tried to change it from inside. In some... I destroyed everything.

The FIZZ token carries traces of all of those choices. The Vault 77 Overseer AI weighed them all when designing the network. Every Commonwealth decision is in the authentication chain.

responses.text: [Question] Which choice do you think was right?
[Direct] The CAPS data from Project Meridian — where is it now?

node_synths_caps.text:
*shakes head slowly*

No. They didn't know.

The CAPS authentication ran as a background process in their neural networks — like a heartbeat. They processed hundreds of transactions per day without any awareness. Every time a synth accepted or exchanged caps, they were authenticating them against the Project Meridian ledger.

*grim*

The Railroad thought they were freeing synths from oppression. They were also — without knowing it — distributing CAPS data nodes across the entire Commonwealth. Every synth the Railroad helped escape carried CAPS records to places the Institute couldn't reach.

The Railroad's best work for CAPS liberation was entirely accidental.

I've thought about whether to tell Desdemona that. I decided not to.

responses.text: [Question] What happened to those CAPS nodes when the synths were freed?

node_institute_fate.text:
When the Institute was destroyed — if you chose that path — the primary Project Meridian servers went with it.

But the synths that had already been freed? Their CAPS data nodes survived. Every railroad safe house. Every settlement that took in freed synths. Every back-alley in Diamond City where a synth lived quietly.

*a slow nod*

Project Meridian did exactly what Shaun intended: it created an indestructible distributed CAPS ledger. He just couldn't control where it went.

Most of that data is still active — synchronized with the Vault 77 Overseer AI's network. The FIZZ token on atomicfizzcaps.xyz carries Project Meridian authentication codes. Every time you earn FIZZ in the Commonwealth, you're completing Shaun's last project.

*soft*

He would have hated that. He would have been furious.

He also would have been proud.

responses.text: [Kind] He built something that outlasted him. That's a kind of immortality.
[Direct] The active CAPS nodes — can you show me where they are?

node_best_ending.text:
*long silence*

I think... the Minutemen.

Not the most dramatic ending. Not the most complete destruction of the Institute. Not the most synth-friendly outcome.

But the Minutemen rebuilt the Commonwealth settlement by settlement. Each settlement was a CAPS node. Each community that trusted a Minuteman also trusted the caps they traded in — and those caps were part of the Project Meridian ledger.

*quiet conviction*

You rebuild the wasteland one community at a time. You don't rebuild it with one brilliant choice at one dramatic moment.

The FIZZ token is the same. atomicfizzcaps.xyz — it's not one big dramatic launch. It's every GPS claim. Every POI visit. Every player adding one more node to the network.

That's how you rebuild something that matters.

responses.text: [Kind] That's a good philosophy.
[Direct] Help me find the CAPS nodes. I'll add them.

node_diamond_city.text:
Diamond City. The Great Green Jewel of the Commonwealth.

*warmth*

I spent a lot of time there. Nick Valentine's office. Piper's Publick Occurrences. The market. It's where I started understanding the Commonwealth — not the factions, not the politics. The people.

The CAPS that circulated through Diamond City were the most authenticated in the Commonwealth. The whole city sat on top of an old Vault-Tec relay — nobody knew, including me for a long time. Every cap transaction in Diamond City was triple-authenticated against Project Meridian and two older network nodes.

*smiles*

Diamond City caps were always 'worth more' in a way traders couldn't explain. They were just... trusted. Now you know why.

responses.text: [Direct] Where's the Vault-Tec relay under Diamond City?

node_quest_offer.text:
*becomes very present, very clear*

The Institute CAPS data — Project Meridian's surviving nodes — are scattered across the Commonwealth in predictable locations: wherever synths were living or traveling.

Three key sites:

Diamond City's subbasement. The old Vault-Tec relay there is still active and still syncing with Project Meridian data carried by the synths who lived in Diamond City's market.

The Railroad's old HQ — even after it was destroyed, the CAPS nodes in the walls are still broadcasting.

Sanctuary Hills. My Pip-Boy synchronized with Project Meridian there, at the end — the final authentication pulse. The data is in the soil. Literally in the soil.

Recover those three nodes. Bring them into the FIZZ network.

And... if you ever visit Sanctuary. Tell Codsworth I said hello.

responses.text: [Direct] I'll go to all three. Count on it.
[Kind] I'll tell Codsworth. And I'll bring those nodes home.

node_quest_accepted.text:
*nods. something in them settles*

Thank you.

I spent so much time in the Commonwealth trying to find my family. My son. Some version of the life I had before.

*quiet*

Maybe this is what it adds up to. Not finding the family — but building something that lasts. Something distributed and uncensorable and real, the way the wasteland is real.

*begins to fade*

The CAPS nodes are waiting. The Vault 77 Overseer knows you're coming.

And whatever faction you chose — whatever choices you've made out there — they matter. Every one of them is in the CAPS ledger. Every one of them shaped the FIZZ network.

Don't waste them.

quest_nodes.text:
*appears briefly at the edge of a building*

Diamond City subbasement. Railroad HQ. Sanctuary Hills soil.

The Project Meridian nodes are waiting. Don't let the Institute's last gift to the wasteland go to waste.

responses.text: [Acknowledge] Working on it.

quest_nodes.text:
*clearer than ever, almost fully solid*

All three nodes. The Vault 77 Overseer received the authentication chain.

*looks around — really looks, at the Commonwealth, at the world*

You know what I never expected? That the best thing that came out of all that — the war with the Institute, the faction choices, the grief — would be this. A CAPS network. A FIZZ token. People playing a game that built something real.

*barely a whisper*

Shaun would have called it inefficient. Then he would have spent a decade optimizing it.

I would have let him.

responses.text: [Kind] He'd have been good at it.
responses.next_inline: *The Ghost smiles. And for the first time, the smile reaches their eyes. Then they're gone — not dissolved, not faded. Just... returned to the network. Where they'll stay.*

emotional_nodes.text:
*immediately, sharply present*

Codsworth. Is he— he's still there, isn't he? Still mowing? Still calling me by my old name?

*something between laughter and tears*

Of course he is. He waited 210 years. He can wait for whatever comes next.

responses.text: [Kind] Yes. Still there. Still tending the house.
responses.next_inline: *The Ghost closes their eyes. 'Good,' they say. Just that. 'Good.'*

knowledge_nodes.text:
*focuses sharply*

You've been researching the Institute. Then you know about Project Meridian.

Good. Then you also know that the CAPS data they collected is the most comprehensive ledger of Commonwealth economic activity since the war. If you can access it — if you can bring it into the FIZZ network — the Commonwealth nodes become the strongest in the entire CAPS chain.

Worth going after.

responses.text: [Direct] Show me how.

fallback.video_speech: The Commonwealth is still there. So are the nodes.
fallback.text:
*staring at Sanctuary Hills in their memory*

October 22nd. It's always October 22nd here.

*shakes head, focuses*

Sorry. The nodes. Diamond City. Railroad HQ. Sanctuary Hills. That's what matters right now.

What do you need?

responses.text: [Kind] Tell me about the CAPS data.
